headline: Council files Bill 102 Wailuku property funding, discusses Bill 88 hotel districts

meeting.summary: Members voted 9–0 to file Bill 102, which would fund buying a Wailuku property. They also discussed Bill 88, which would create H3 and H4 hotel districts for A1 and A2 apartment-district properties, and a budget amendment directing up to $3 million to Maui Economic Opportunity Inc.
meeting.recap: The chair announced that former council member Rick Medina had passed away.[[0:05:06]] A testifier urged the council to pass Bill 88, which creates H3 and H4 zoning, unchanged.[[0:16:20]] Another testifier opposed Bills 89, 90 and 91, citing concerns about ancestral burials on the land.[[0:52:38]] A council member moved to file, or set aside, Bill 102, which would fund buying a Wailuku property.[[2:00:15]] That motion passed 9–0.[[2:06:52]] Bill 88 would create H3 and H4 hotel districts that conditionally allow vacation rentals being phased out of apartment districts.[[2:09:35]] A budget amendment directs up to $3 million to Maui Economic Opportunity Inc. for an Upcountry wildfire rebuild pilot program.[[4:06:19]]
meeting.next: A county attorney said they would move a clarifying ordinance on open space fund appropriations as quickly as possible.

issues.oneLine: Bill 88 would create H3 and H4 hotel districts for properties now in A1 and A2 apartment districts.
issues.why: Vacation rental use is being phased out of apartment districts, and the new districts would conditionally allow it.
issues.next: A county attorney said a related tax question could be looked into before second reading.
issues.brief: A legal advisor said the list of possibly qualifying properties is informational and does not stop others from applying.[[#1]] Members amended the bill so expansion of the existing total square footage of the floor area is prohibited.[[#2]] The roll call recorded seven ayes.[[#3]]
